title: The most dangerous sentence in the Bible isn’t violent.
paragraphs:
The most dangerous sentence in the Bible isn’t violent.
It’s confident.
“Look what I built.”
That’s what Book of Daniel records when Nebuchadnezzar II stood over Babylon — gold walls, hanging gardens, power echoing his name.
He forgot one thing.
Who gave him breath.

Before the echo of his pride faded, heaven answered.
His mind left him.
The king became like cattle.
Read Daniel 4:30 and Daniel 4:32 — the fall was instant.
Here’s the part we don’t preach enough:
God didn’t destroy him.
He restored him.
When Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven, sanity returned. Authority returned. Influence returned.

Pride makes you forget Who gave it.
Grace reminds you.

Centuries later, another King stood — not over a kingdom of gold, but under a sky growing dark. Jesus Christ had every right to boast. Instead, Philippians 2:8 says He humbled Himself to death on a cross.

One said, “Look what I built.”
The Other said, “Father, forgive them.”

One built brick.
The Other built redemption.
Mga kapatid — what rooftop are you standing on right now?

Your career?
Your platform?
Your ministry metrics?
Before heaven has to whisper, kneel.
Because everything we call “mine” is borrowed glory.
And those who walk in pride — He is able to humble (Daniel 4:37).
That’s still the pattern.
